about: Questions only the owner can settle (fix list #36). Curated by Claude; shown in the app at #questions (data/questions.json, open ones only). The owner's answers come back as an answers file from the app and tools/pipeline/owner_answers.py turns them into verified owner change events (effect 'set') or a follow-up list for Claude (effect 'followup'). A question is closed once collection/owner_answers.jsonl holds an answer for its id.

questions.ask: How many stars are on token T001 (the 20 play token with GR)?
questions.why: Its record says 13 stars; its twin T002 has 15. If they differ they are two different kinds.

options.followup: T001 has 13 stars, T002 has 15: split DE.X.spielmarke-20-gr into two types.
T001 has 15 stars like T002: fix T001's notes (13 -> 15); one type is right.

options.label: Another number
options.followup: T001 star count from the owner (see the answer text): fix the notes; split the type if it is not 15.

questions.ask: Turn over C153, the 2008 UK 10 pence. Does the back show a crowned lion, or a piece of the Royal Shield?
questions.why: 2008 had both designs. The record lists the lion type.

options.label: Crowned lion
options.followup: C153 is the lion (KM#989): clear the curation item.

options.label: Part of a shield
options.followup: C153 moved to GB.KM.1110 (Dent shield): fix its mintage text and value.

questions.ask: East Caribbean coins are filed under the code EC, which is really Ecuador's code. Switch East Caribbean to XC?
questions.why: It only changes the short code in serial numbers (EC-... to XC-...), before the one-time serial renumbering.

options.label: Yes, use XC
options.followup: Owner: East Caribbean -> XC. Re-key issuer EC (East Caribbean) to XC before the serial reassignment; Ecuador keeps EC.

options.label: No, keep EC
options.followup: Owner: keep EC for East Caribbean. Note it in the serial plan.

questions.ask: Your Mercury dime album (A006): from your page photos it has 77 holes, but the record says about 80. Is 77 right?
questions.why: The 80 was an estimate. Only you can lower a count.

options.label: Yes, 77
options.followup: A006 slots_total 77 (owner): clear slots_total_approx.

options.label: No
options.followup: A006 hole count from the owner (see answer text).

questions.ask: Do you have two UK 5 pence coins dated 1992?
questions.why: C169 (from the ledger) and C275 (added later from a photo) are both 1992 5p. They may be the same coin logged twice.

options.label: Yes, two
options.followup: Owner has two 1992 5p: C169 and C275 are both real; nothing to merge.

options.label: No, only one
options.followup: C169 and C275 are the same coin: retire one record (keep C275's photo on the survivor).

options.label: Not sure
options.followup: Owner unsure about two 1992 5p: check at Phase 2.

questions.ask: Please take a phone photo of C140's map side (Spain 2008 1 cent) and drop it in the STAGING folder.
questions.why: Spain's 1 cent changed design in 2010; the map side helps confirm the catalog number.

options.label: Done, photo sent
options.followup: Owner says the C140 map-side photo is in STAGING: file and read it.

questions.ask: Turn over C023, the 1918 iron 20 in the oak wreath. Is the other side a crowned double-headed eagle with a shield on its chest?
questions.why: The side we have matches Austria's 1918 iron 20 heller (KM#2826) exactly: a 20 in an oak wreath, the date below, no lettering. No German 20 pfennig was struck in 1918, so it was moved from Germany to Austria on 2026-10-23 (found by Gemini, checked by Claude). A German city token would show words (a city name) instead of the eagle.

options.label: Yes, the eagle
options.followup: C023 is Austria's 20 heller (KM#2826), owner-confirmed: clear the question.

options.label: No, it has words
options.followup: C023 is not the Austrian coin: re-file it as the German city notgeld the words name (see the answer text).

options.label: I'll send a photo
options.followup: Owner will drop a photo of C023's other side in STAGING.

questions.ask: On C238, the 1973 D West German 2 mark, whose name is written next to the portrait: KONRAD ADENAUER or THEODOR HEUSS?
questions.why: They are two different coins (KM#124 Adenauer, KM#A127 Heuss) with different mintages; the record lists both.

options.label: Konrad Adenauer
options.followup: C238 is KM#124 (Numista N#844): drop KM#A127 from DE.KM.124; 1973 D mintage 10,393,000 stays.

options.label: Theodor Heuss
options.followup: C238 is KM#A127 (Numista N#1935): new type DE.KM.A127, move C238, 1973 D mintage 10,379,000.

options.label: I'll send a photo
options.followup: Owner will drop a photo of C238's portrait side in STAGING.

questions.ask: On C088, the 1957 dime, look on the torch side, left of the torch near the bottom. Is there a small D?
questions.why: No letter means Philadelphia (160,160,000 struck); D means Denver (113,354,330). The record can't tell yet.

options.label: No letter
options.followup: C088 is 1957 Philadelphia: set mintage 160,160,000 with a PCGS citation.

questions.ask: On C064, the Malta 2008 1 euro, is there a small F on the Maltese (cross) side?
questions.why: Catalogues list the 2008 Maltese 1 euro as struck in Paris with an F mint mark.

options.label: Yes, an F
options.followup: C064 mint mark F (Paris) recorded: tidy the mint text.

options.label: No letter
options.followup: C064 has no visible F: note it in the record.

questions.ask: C073 is a tube of 26 1976 quarters. Keep it as one mixed lot, or sort it into no-letter and D piles?
questions.why: Philadelphia and Denver struck different numbers (809,784,016 and 860,118,839), so one mintage can't describe a mixed tube.

options.label: Keep it as one lot
options.followup: C073 stays one mixed lot; mintage stays empty with both figures in the text.

options.label: I'll sort it
options.free: How many with D, how many without?
options.followup: Split C073 into two lots by mint (see the answer text).

Create the UK 1932 penny (KM#838) from NOID_UnitedKingdom_1922_1Penny_rev.jpg (rename the photo).

questions.ask: Australia 1943 threepence (C031): look closely around the date 43. Is there a small D or S letter, or no letter?
questions.why: Muse read no letter, the record says S (San Francisco); the phone photo is too small to tell. It decides the mintage: plain 1943 (Melbourne), 1943 D (Denver) or 1943 S (San Francisco).

options.label: An S
options.followup: C031 stays 1943 S: settle D0128 for the record.

options.label: A D
options.followup: C031 is 1943 D (Denver): fix its mint text and mintage; settle D0128 (neither).

options.label: No letter
options.followup: C031 is plain 1943 (Melbourne): fix its mint text and mintage; settle D0128 for Muse.

options.label: Can't tell
options.followup: Leave D0128 open for the pro photo.
